reason: A loose count of the cells in a hair or costa. 'few' alone was rejected in the previous review, so this belongs to the count pattern, not a term. PATO_0001993 multicellular covers only the bare reading.
Two different meanings: a shiny surface on the fruit and a hard, see-through endosperm. Without the context neither reading is safe.
The shape is a Y. 'Inverted' only gives which way it faces, and the examples describe a cross-section.
In botany an oval is broadly elliptic, so a long oval is an elliptic outline. PATO puts 'oval' under ovate, which is egg-shaped and does not fit a long outline.

label: musk-scented
definition: An odorous quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a heavy, sweetish odour like that of musk.
reason: A distinct smell used for flowers and fruit pulp, sitting beside the existing FLOPO smell classes (sweet-scented FLOPO:0991016, spicy-scented FLOPO:0991017).
'Racemed heads/catkins' means the units are arranged along an unbranched axis like a raceme.
A racemose main axis with cymose side branches is exactly how the thyrse-like class is defined.
'Half an oval' is used for a 3-D hypanthium and for flat corolla lobes. No shape term fits both, and it is too rare to justify a new one.
The shape is cylindrical. 'Slenderly' only adds that it is narrow.

target: new: quality of a named part (X-leaved)
reason: The statement is about the leaves of the shoot (leaf PO_0025034 + decreased size), not the shoot itself. The word should be split into part and quality, not given its own term.
One use is a lichen apothecium, which is not a plant part. The other is an aril whose pointed base looks like a stalk, a figure of speech. No sound plant quality is left.
A bare number taken out of 'three or four times dissected/branching'. On its own it is a fragment, not a quality.
PO has no term for a pit, and 'pitted' was mapped to foveate in the previous review, so 'without pits' is not foveate. Wall pits in wood cells fit this reading less well.
Says the seed has no strophiole, and PO has a strophiole class.
'Echinate' was mapped to PATO spiny in the previous review. PO has no general spine class, so negating spiny is the cleanest reading.
Ocellate means marked with eye-like spots, a kind of spotting. With only two statements, the existing term is better than a new one.

label: ancipital
definition: A flattened quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being flattened in cross-section with two thin, sharp or narrowly winged opposite edges.
reason: A standard botanical term for two-edged stems, peduncles and bracts. PATO flattened does not include the two sharp edges, and PATO winged (PATO_0104354) is too strong.
An inflorescence shaped like a fascicle has its flowers in a close cluster from about one point, which is what fascicled means.
Translucent already means letting some light through. 'Semi-' adds nothing that can be annotated.
Annulus means ring. PATO lists 'annular' as a synonym of ring shaped.
A piece cut from the colour range 'bright mid- to deep green'. The colour is in the full phrase, not in this piece.
Compares the width and depth of the same sinus.
Two values on one bearer: flattened (PATO_0002254) and conical (PATO_0002021).
'Digitately' (finger-like) and 'discoid' (disc-shaped) do not make sense together for a blade. It looks like a garbled 'digitately lobed' or a fragment.
Two surface values on one bearer: spiny (PATO_0001365) and scabrous (FLOPO:0991058).
Two shape values: elongated and nearly arrow-shaped (PATO_0001881).
Probably a misspelling of extrorse, but here it describes leaf lobes turned outward. FLOPO:0991165 extrorse is defined for parts facing away from the centre of a flower, so it does not fit.
'When furled' gives the state of the spathe under which another statement holds. It does not describe the spathe itself.
A misspelling of granular-puberulent: two values, granular (PATO_0001759) and puberulous (FLOPO:0991049).
Describes the leaf as covered in fine grain-like specks, which is a colour pattern of spots.
